Our universe might be chock-full of cosmic wonder, but you can observe only a fraction of astronomical phenomena with your naked eye. Meteor showers, natural fireworks that streak brightly across the night sky, are one of them.

The latest shower is called the Leonids. It produces some of the fastest meteors, at about 44 miles per second, with bright and colorful streaks. But the observation rate is low. This year, skywatchers might see fewer than three meteors per hour. And the moon will be 41 percent full, the American Meteor Society said, so its light may obscure fainter streaks for part of the night.

Users may also opt in to share HealthKit metrics such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results, to assess how personal health data enhances relevance and understanding, as well as how AI tools can help patients prepare for appointments with their physicians.

paras: Apple today announced the launch of the Apple Health AI Usage Study in the United States, a virtual research study and associated app designed to advance the understanding of how people interact with conversational health AI tools.1 By examining what drives user trust, the quality of responses, comprehension, and everyday health actions, the study aims to inform the responsible design of health AI experiences for Apple and the industry.

The study is designed from the ground up with privacy protections, transparency, and clinical guardrails, and study data will not be used to train AI models. Participants retain control over whether to share any HealthKit metrics or survey responses, and Apple has implemented security measures to protect the study data it maintains, as well as the confidentiality of participants’ information. The study app features safety guardrails that are intended to detect certain concerning questions and suggest that a participant follow up with a provider or other resources if needed.

The Apple Health AI Usage Study is open to up to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older across the United States. To join, participants must have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro or later) running iOS 26 or later. Download the study app to learn more about the study and choose to enroll.

paras: Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached Spain’s Canary Islands by boat over the past two days, Spain’s maritime rescue service said on Sunday.

The archipelago off northwest Africa is a major entry point for migrants, mainly from West Africa, attempting the dangerous Atlantic crossing in makeshift boats. More than 13,000 of the just over 28,000 people who arrived in Spain by sea between January and the end of October landed in the Canary Islands, according to the Interior Ministry.

Spain declared a migration emergency on the islands on Tuesday following a rise in arrivals in recent weeks, particularly from sub-Saharan Africa. The country is due to hold an early general election in two weeks.

paras: As tiny pieces of the comet fizzle in the atmosphere, they create meteors that can be seen blazing across the night sky.

This year, the shower is expected to peak overnight from Monday through Tuesday, when Earth passes through the densest part of the debris trail, according to the American Meteor Society. pg:https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2.desc: Mayor axes strategic response group that cracked down on protesters and announces new community safety division

New York — A controversial New York Police Department unit accused of using excessive force against protesters has been disbanded, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch announced Monday, fulfilling a key campaign promise from the mayor to separate protest policing from counterterrorism.

Along with the elimination of the Strategic Response Group, certain aggressive crowd-management tactics are now banned and new, dialogue-focused units will be established in the NYPD and the Mayor’s Office of Community Safety to ensure a coordinated response to protests, the mayor and commissioner said in a statement.

The new civilian-led “Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division” will not have weapons or arresting powers and will work with a new NYPD unit – The First Amendment Support Team – to prepare for and respond to protests. Both units will work with a new Patrol Support Division within the NYPD staffed by vetted officers who will receive specialized crowd control management training.

paras: COP31 entered its second week of negotiations in Antalya, Türkiye. The draft decision released on Monday, November 16, proposes increased climate finance for developing countries and accelerated action to move away from fossil fuels. Meanwhile, negotiators began a new phase of ministerial consultations aimed at resolving outstanding political disagreements ahead of the conference's scheduled conclusion on 20 November.

The 18-page draft, prepared under the COP31 presidency, calls for tripling annual adaptation finance for developing countries to at least $120 billion by 2035. It calls on developed countries to increase their collective contributions and establish a roadmap with measurable milestones to monitor progress. It also seeks a better balance between adaptation and mitigation funding within the broader objective of mobilising at least $300 billion annually by 2035.

On energy, the draft advocates an immediate and accelerated transition away from fossil fuels in a "just, orderly and equitable" manner, alongside the elimination of inefficient fossil fuel subsidies. It also proposes increasing electricity's share of final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, tripling global renewable energy capacity and doubling the annual rate of energy efficiency improvements by 2030. Additional initiatives include the reduction of methane emissions via strengthened monitoring and the elimination of routine flaring and venting.

pg:https://www.natureworldnews.com/artic.desc: COP31 in Antalya enters its last week with thousands protesting and nearly 200 nations still split on fossil fuels, adaptation money and electrification.

Police estimated that more than 7,000 people joined Saturday's march in downtown Antalya, AFP reported. It was the largest demonstration since the summit opened on November 9. pg:https://www.newsweek.com/what-elon-mu.desc: SpaceX’s historic Starship catch marks a major step toward the Moon, but a crucial hurdle remains.
paras: The upper-stage spacecraft returned to SpaceX’s Starbase facility in South Texas on Saturday, November 14, after spending approximately 22 hours in space and completing 14 orbits of Earth. As it approached the ground, Starship slowed itself, moved upright, and descended between two giant mechanical arms attached to its launch tower. Deep Space Network — NASA’s web of giant antennas across three continents that ensures Earth “faces” the spacecraft at all times — did not record a radio signal from the interstellar explorer during two scheduled interaction attempts made 24 hours apart. The signal was back two days later, on October 20. NASA engineers have only partly ascertained the reason for the glitch, and the probe continues.

This was not Earth’s first loss of contact with Voyager 1. In December 1979, two years after its launch in 1977, NASA lost touch with the spacecraft after a flight-altering manoeuvre. More recently, in 2023 and 2024, Voyager 1 faced similar snags. But barring such minor hiccups, which are bound to happen in any long-distance relationship, the spacecraft’s longevity is testimony to its endurance.

The team started with a list of 675 facilities from a commercial database based on news reports, company statements, and satellite imagery. They dropped any that didn’t have a reported electrical capacity or that they couldn’t verify was a suitably large building with the expected cooling and electrical connection equipment. That reduced the list to 403 data centers with an average electrical capacity of about 40 megawatts.

As I have prepared for these negotiations, I’ve been reflecting on the gap between the science and the political debate in Britain. Early predictions by the Met Office indicate that 2027 will surpass 2024 as the hottest year on record globally as El Niño rips through the Pacific. This is a sobering reality. And yet, the Conservatives and Reform UK want to bury their heads in the sand and break the consensus on delivering net zero. But we know sustained climate action can work.

Yes, the world will overshoot 1.5C of global heating in the coming years. But without the Paris agreement, the world would have been on track for a 4C increase. International commitments, finance and adaptation are working, and multilateralism has never been more vital to our future. paras: TRENTON, NJ – Today, the Pan-American Health Organization has officially revoked our nation’s measles elimination status. The loss of this status in the U.S. is a sobering reminder that decades of public health progress can be undone in a short fraction of that time and should not be taken for granted.

Losing elimination status represents a significant setback – and a preventable one. Public health and medical experts have repeatedly raised concerns about declining vaccination rates. When less than 95% of a community is vaccinated against measles, the virus can spread quickly. According to the most recent data, only 92% of children in New Jersey have received the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine by 24 months of age, on par with 91.4% nationally. According to the latest data, vaccination coverage among kindergartners in the U.S. is 92.4% for MMR vaccine, below herd immunity.

paras: Few things in cinema are more subjective than deciding who was the best, or worst, James Bond. The same goes, broadly speaking, for choosing between actors who have played the same character. Such debates can lead to lively and fiercely contested arguments... except in obvious cases such as Superman (Christopher Reeve) and, to open another can of worms, Batman (George Clooney, though he was saddled with the worst suit and the worst script in the worst film).

There have been several James Bonds. By the official canon, there have been seven actors in the role, although an eighth, David Niven, played him in the 1967 Casino Royale, a film made outside the Eon Productions umbrella, the company that held the screen rights to Ian Fleming’s creation. The first actor to bring Bond to the screen was the American actor (sacrilege!) Barry Nelson in the 47-minute television adaptation Casino Royale (1954), broadcast as part of CBS’s Climax! series.

Incidentally, even Sean Connery stepped outside the official canon when he played the secret agent for a seventh time in Never Say Never Again (1983), produced by Warner Bros., while Eon had Roger Moore under contract. It is also striking to look at the list of actors who came close to playing Bond, or turned down the role altogether: Cary Grant (who would have been magnificent), Adam West (the Batman of the classic TV series), Patrick McGoohan, Burt Reynolds, Sam Neill (who would have landed the part had Dalton declined it), Henry Cavill and Sam Worthington (the two finalists who lost out when Daniel Craig won the role), and now Nicholas Hoult, who lost the role to Robert Pattinson.

paras: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang broke his silence after resigning from the company following revelations of multiple affairs, saying he'd be willing to return as its CEO.

He added, "If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."

Late Tuesday, however, Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones said the company's board doesn't intend to rehire Huang as chief executive. The company's search for a new chief is underway, he added, while noting that the board has "every confidence" in Kress' ability to lead the company. Jones said the company is considering both internal and external candidates to replace Huang.
